content.text:
Read-only audit complete. The current mobile app is deliberately a small Android-first client: direct BYOK streaming, `AsyncStorage` session/artifact state, SecureStore keys, three inline card types, and offline plan/map/quiz generation. The web product is materially broader: Pi agent + tool loop, IndexedDB event/artifact stores, fork/share sessions, OpenUI/media/decks/SRS, authenticated course operations, and server-owned Not Organic access.

The parity path should therefore be a platform architecture program, not a port of `useKeatingAgent.tsx`.

## Current seams and non-negotiables

| Area | Mobile today | Web source of truth / required direction |
|---|---|---|
| Agent | `mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx` calls `provider-client.ts` directly; no tool calls | `web/src/hooks/useKeatingAgent.tsx`, `web/src/keating/browser-tools.ts`, `capabilities.ts`, `security/*` |
| State | one `PersistedAppState` v1 blob in AsyncStorage | sessions plus `web/src/keating/storage.ts` (artifact/event/SRS/learner stores) |
| Cards | quiz/question/goal tags in `interactive-tags.ts` | OpenUI streaming/renderer plus quiz, decks, image, animation, map components |
| Sessions | flat, local sessions only | `types/session.ts`, `use-sessions.ts`, tree/forks, `shared-sessions.ts`, portable export |
| Courses | absent | `web/src/courses/*`, `web/server/api/courses/*`, server-side product session |
| Settings | raw API keys and five providers | BYOK/OAuth/cloud models/Not Organic, web search, voice, learning preferences |
| Visual system | `mobile/src/constants/theme.ts`, dark only | `web/panda.config.ts`, semantic CSS tokens, web light/dark themes |
| Native config | Android only, portrait only | `mobile/app.json`, generated Android project; no iOS product configuration |

Do not import the web agent, IndexedDB storage, Pi runtime, browser tools, DOM renderers, or desktop P2P code into Metro. `mobile/src/lib/keating-core.ts` is the correct pattern: shared only when dependency-free.

## Dependency-ordered implementation plan

1. Establish portable contracts before changing screens.

Create a workspace package such as `packages/keating-learner-contract/` containing only TypeScript/Zod/pure logic:

- normalized `LearnerMessage`, `LearnerSession`, `SessionMetadata`, branch/fork fields, feedback, goals, question checks, quiz results, decks/card reviews, artifact descriptors, provider references, share snapshots, and migration envelopes;
- versioned portable export/import and deterministic merge/deduplication rules;
- tool schema/result/event protocol (`tool-call`, incremental text, tool result, artifact emitted, recoverable error), including stable idempotency keys;
- the current interactive-tag normalization plus a platform-neutral OpenUI segment contract.

Adapt, rather than immediately replace:

- mobile: `mobile/src/lib/types.ts`, `storage.ts`, `interactive-tags.ts`, `learning-artifacts.ts`, `state/KeatingProvider.tsx`;
- web: `web/src/types/session.ts`, `keating/portable-data.ts`, `keating/share-contract.ts`, `keating/share-codec.ts`, `keating/openui/{types,segments}.ts`, and pure parts of `keating/storage.ts`.

Gate: fixture round-trips in web and mobile preserve a forked session, deck review, goal, graded quiz, attachment metadata, and unsupported-version refusal. No keys, OAuth credentials, raw DPoP material, or local workspace files may be exported.

2. Replace the mobile blob with a local durable repository and migration path.

Add a mobile repository facade, not more provider logic in `KeatingProvider`:

- `mobile/src/lib/storage/` with versioned migrations from `keating.mobile.state.v1`;
- SQLite for queryable sessions/messages/artifacts/decks/reviews/operation queue (AsyncStorage is not a durable large transcript/media database); SecureStore remains credentials-only;
- file-backed attachment cache with quota/eviction and referential cleanup;
- a local operation journal for retries and future cloud/course sync;
- a temporary importer that converts existing sessions, saved notes, feedback, persona, and provider settings atomically and keeps the old blob until migration success.

Keep course data distinct from personal learner state: course mutations already have a `baseRevision` and operation IDs in `web/src/courses/contracts.ts` / `operations.ts`; reuse that optimistic-concurrency model.

Gate: upgrade, interrupted migration, downgrade refusal, delete/export/import, quota, and offline-restart tests. Existing user state survives an app upgrade byte-for-byte at the semantic level.

3. Build a portable agent/tool loop with platform adapters.

Define a native `AgentRunner` that consumes the shared event contract and exposes the same recoverable turn model as the web. Preserve `provider-client.ts` as the BYOK transport adapter, but add tool-call streaming/parsing and a tool executor.

Split tools into adapters:

- pure/on-device: quiz/question grading, learner profile/goals, decks/SRS, deterministic plan/map/quiz, local artifact save/search;
- authenticated server APIs: courses, hosted provider, share publication, cloud backup, generated images/animations, grading needing a model;
- explicitly unavailable: browser NodePod/host filesystem/bash/workspace editing, until a native-compatible remote sandbox protocol exists.

Use the same schema validation/result rules currently in `web/src/keating/browser-tools/shared.ts`. Register every truly supported baseline tool on the initial turn; do not reintroduce capability activation cascades. Unknown, secret-bearing, untrusted, or mutation-capable operations remain fail-closed and surfaced with Retry, Sign in, Settings, or Review actions.

Do not attempt to run `@scelar/nodepod` or the browser runtime package on React Native. If native workspace work is later desired, speak the `packages/browser-agent-runtime` RPC contract to the existing remote/host backend; it is a separate capability, not local sandboxing.

Gate: scripted provider fixtures prove text/tool interleaving, canceled turns, malformed arguments, tool exceptions, offline capability messaging, retry after app backgrounding, and exactly-once local tool effects.

4. Bring session, branch, share, and sync parity in layers.

- Add branches and alternatives to mobile session metadata/UI using the portable session contract; port the pure tree/metadata logic from `web/src/components/session-tree.ts` and `hooks/session-metadata.ts`.
- Implement native deep links (`keating://` plus universal links) for `/s/:id`; reuse the share schema, but move base64/compression behind a universal codec—browser `btoa`/`atob` are not a native dependency boundary.
- Support existing hosted `/api/share` only as an explicitly public transcript share with the same warning/consent semantics. Local-short links cannot be represented as useful cross-device mobile links; label them device-local.
- Add optional authenticated cloud backup/sync after local storage is reliable. It needs server-issued identity, per-record version/idempotency/merge semantics, encrypted-at-rest content, conflict UI, and an offline queue. Do not describe desktop Hypercore/Hyperswarm as mobile sync; use a relay/backend or ship no cross-device sync.

Gate: fork on web → export/import/open on mobile; mobile-generated public share opens on web; collisions produce a reviewable conflict, never silent loss; offline queued edits replay once after reconnect.

5. Implement learner content parity before decorative parity.

Add native renderers/screens in this order:

- rich Markdown/math/code/link safety and OpenUI atomic segments;
- `Question`, `Quiz`, `Goal`, `StudyPlan`, feedback/retry cards;
- Flashcard/deck browser and review flow with the web `flashcard-types.ts`, `srs.ts`, `CardReviewRecord`, and Anki compatibility model;
- learner profile, evidence gaps, Coming Up/due review, review history;
- artifact browser/detail/export with typed artifacts—not just copied assistant text;
- images, maps, documents, and media;
- course-owned quiz/openui/lesson-plan/map/animation artifacts.

For maps, render sanitized precomputed SVG or native SVG primitives; Mermaid DOM rendering is not portable. For Hyperframes, prefer a server-rendered video/image or a narrowly sandboxed WebView bridge with navigation disabled and an explicit trust policy; do not execute arbitrary model-produced HTML/JS as a first-class native capability. For local documents/media, use platform file viewers and attachment cache, not Base64 in session records.

Likely native dependencies require deliberate evaluation/addition: Expo SQLite, FileSystem, Sharing, DocumentPicker/ImagePicker, WebBrowser/AuthSession, Image, and possibly `react-native-webview`/SVG. Their config-plugin changes mean fresh Android and iOS prebuilds.

Gate: an end-to-end learner scenario can create and complete an OpenUI question, grade and revisit a quiz, review a due card, save/open/export an artifact, and resume after force-kill—all offline where the capability is local.

6. Add provider, account, and course parity with the correct trust boundary.

Keep direct BYOK as an explicit local mode. Add separate account/hosted modes:

- mobile OAuth uses authorization-code PKCE with `expo-auth-session`/deep-link callback and a native secure credential store;
- never copy browser `localStorage` OAuth behavior directly;
- Not Organic access must remain server-owned. Mobile sends a server-issued product session/access token to same-origin/mobile API routes; the server resolves identity, holds the five-minute access token/DPoP key, and enforces reservation/idempotency. The client must not supply an account ID or product assertion;
- expose provider errors as recoverable state, preserving a draft/turn—no success-looking hosted fallback;
- port model selection/capability presentation from `web/src/lib/provider-models.ts`, `keating/providers/capabilities.ts`, and settings components, while marking mobile-unavailable features honestly;
- add course account bootstrap, list/workspace/join/invite, files, artifacts, comments/reactions, realtime refresh, assignments/submissions/reviews, consent, and teacher access by using the existing `web/src/courses/client.ts` contracts and server routes.

The existing course session is an HTTP-only cookie (`web/server/utils/course-session.ts`). It is appropriate for web/local development, but not sufficient as the native auth design. Add a dedicated mobile session exchange/authorization middleware that validates a signed server credential before it maps to `requireCourseProductSession`; do not accept a caller-provided identity.

Gate: a hosted user signs in, can resume a course on another device, observes role/teacher-consent restrictions server-side, and loses access cleanly after sign-out/token expiry. Local-development Courses remain usable through the full server, not a `VITE_NOTORGANIC_ENABLED` inference.

7. Make visual parity systematic, then validate actual devices.

Create a source-neutral token manifest generated from—or made authoritative alongside—`web/panda.config.ts`: semantic color modes, typography, spacing, radii, elevation, state colors, icons, motion durations, and touch-target rules. Generate/export a TypeScript native token module consumed by `mobile/src/constants/theme.ts`; do not hand-maintain divergent hex values.

Refactor mobile primitives (`Screen`, `Buttons`, message/cards, tabs) before feature screens. Add light mode/system preference, dynamic type, reduced motion, safe areas, keyboard/inset behavior, RTL/localization checks, scroll fallback for every long panel, and 44pt minimum targets. Keep the navigation native rather than reproducing desktop panel geometry.

Update `mobile/app.json` / `eas.json` for iOS: bundle identifier, tablet/orientation decision, universal-link domains, permission usage strings, associated domains, icons/splash, build profiles, and privacy declarations. Validate Android large text, predictive back, low-memory process death, attachment permissions, 10.0.2.2 development networking, and release network-security behavior. iOS must be tested on a physical device or EAS build; source compilation is not iOS acceptance.

## Verification and release gates

- Unit/property tests: contracts, migrations, tool schemas, idempotence, share codec, sync merge, SRS, permissions and redaction.
- Component tests: React Native Testing Library for all renderers and recovery controls; retain the current `mobile/test/*` streaming/card coverage.
- API contract tests: mobile client fixtures against `/api/share`, hosted mobile auth, `/api/courses`, files, realtime, and Not Organic error variants.
- Build checks: `keating:mobile-check`, `keating:mobile-export`, clean Android prebuild/APK, and an iOS EAS or local prebuild/build.
- Device acceptance: Android physical arm64 plus iPhone, compact and large screens, dark/light, no network, slow network, auth expiry, background/resume/force-kill, portrait keyboard, and screen-reader traversal.
- Cross-surface acceptance: identical fixture course/session/deck/artifact has the same visible learner state on web and native; responsive screenshots are reviewed rather than inferred from unit/build success.

Primary risks are scope coupling (web’s local-first agent code is browser-bound), native auth incorrectly inheriting cookie assumptions, arbitrary animation HTML in WebView, data-loss during schema replacement, AsyncStorage capacity, and claiming P2P or hosted provider parity without a real native authenticated execution path.

M1 is correctly blocked on C1’s Luna acceptance. The current mobile store cannot meet M1 yet: it is one loose AsyncStorage JSON blob, has no migration/repository layer, and `expo-sqlite` is neither installed nor referenced.

### Current persistence

| Area | Current durable form | M1 gap |
|---|---|---|
| Sessions/messages | `keating.mobile.state.v1`: flat sessions with user/assistant messages and numeric timestamps | No branches, parent/fork references, models/tool messages, ISO contract timestamps, or atomic writes |
| Artifacts | Assistant/generated text records inside same blob | Not C1 typed artifacts; no `updatedAt`, attachment refs, portable validation, or transactional delete |
| Goals | Inline tag/card state | Card state is in-memory only; restart loses progress |
| Questions/quizzes | Quiz/form reports may enter transcript | No durable question checks, quiz results, partial credits, pending grades, or idempotent submission record |
| Decks/reviews | None | No deck/card/SRS review persistence |
| Learner profile | Helpful/missed counters only | No C1 learner profile |
| Settings | Provider settings in blob; persona in a separate AsyncStorage key | Preserve as local nonportable settings; keys remain only in SecureStore |

The legacy loader only checks `schemaVersion === 1` after `JSON.parse`; it has no shape validation, recovery journal, migration, quota, import/export, or serialization ordering. The 120 ms debounced blob writer also cannot give M1’s force-kill/atomicity guarantees.

### Safe M1 write set

- New `mobile/src/lib/learner-repository/**`:
  - schema, migration journal, legacy-v1 adapter, SQLite repository, portable import/export adapter, quota accounting.
- New focused repository/migration tests under `mobile/test/`.
- `mobile/package.json` for `expo-sqlite`; coordinate the root lockfile change with I1/coordinator.
- A narrow persistence integration seam in `KeatingProvider` must be explicitly assigned/serialized with the coordinator. Do not alter provider streaming, card/screens, C1, or mobile UI work as part of M1.

`expo-sqlite` is absent, so adding it requires Expo’s SDK-compatible installer, native prebuild, and a rebuilt dev client/APK before real SQLite verification. Metro resolution of the new workspace contract package also needs an Android bundle smoke test.

### Repository target and migration

Use SQLite `user_version` plus a migration journal/meta table, with ISO-UTC C1 records:

- `sessions`, `messages`, `branches`
- `artifacts` and attachment metadata
- `goals`, `goal_steps`, `question_checks`
- `quiz_results` (answers, partial credits, pending grades)
- `decks`, `deck_cards`, `card_reviews`
- singleton `learner_profile`
- local-only `app_settings`/legacy feedback, excluded from portable exports

Convert every existing session into one active primary branch; convert numeric dates to UTC strings; use created time as legacy artifact updated time; preserve provider settings and feedback locally, but never export SecureStore keys or provider credentials.

The cross-store migration must be resumable rather than pretending AsyncStorage and SQLite share a transaction:

1. Read and validate the old blob; retain a recoverable legacy snapshot/journal.
2. In one exclusive SQLite transaction, upsert the converted records and write `legacy-v1-complete`.
3. On restart, rerun incomplete work idempotently; if SQLite is complete but AsyncStorage remains, remove only the legacy key.
4. Update React state only after commit. Never delete the source blob before the durable completion marker.

All logical writes, delete cascades, and imports belong in exclusive SQLite transactions. Validate import envelopes through C1 before merging; compute the merged result before writing, reject conflicts without partial writes, and exclude all provider/session credentials. Define a product quota before implementation; enforce it inside the write transaction and expose a recoverable quota error. Native file-picker/share UX is a later integration dependency because no file import/export package is currently present.

1. Add SQLite dependency and repository driver seam; confirm Metro/native availability.
2. Implement schema/meta/journal, read-only snapshot, and atomic CRUD for sessions/messages/artifacts.
3. Add resumable v1 migration, preserving every legacy session/note/settings value.

5. Add C1 portable export/import/merge adapter.
6. Integrate hydration/write commands through the assigned `KeatingProvider` seam; keep M2 streaming and M3 UI work separate.

- Pure tests: legacy conversion, C1 fixture round-trip, malformed/secret export rejection, import conflict rollback, deterministic ordering.
- SQLite/device tests: interrupted migration at every journal phase, atomic multi-record write, delete cascade, quota rollback, offline restart/force-kill resume.
- Package gates: mobile tests/typecheck, then `keating:mobile-export` and rebuilt APK.
- Physical Android: migrate real v1 state offline, kill/relaunch, verify branches/artifacts/reviews survive, export/import without duplication. iPhone/native UI acceptance remains broader M3/M5 work.
